Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset: tiny transparent portfolio character illustration.
Input image 1 is the exact edit target. Preserve its extremely simple design and the same sparse, rounded, gently hand-wobbled peacock-green #086B68 outline.
Change ONLY the doll's posture and viewpoint: she must unmistakably be LYING FLAT ON HER BACK, reclining away from the viewer on an invisible horizontal surface, with gentle perspective foreshortening. The current image looks like an upright doll merely tipped sideways. Redraw the pose in a low three-quarter overhead view, so the doll's long axis lies mostly across the picture: head at upper left, little feet at lower right, roughly 20–25 degrees below the horizontal. Her head, neck, torso and feet must remain anatomically aligned along that SAME axis, no twisted neck or head facing a different direction. Face and apron tilt backward into the same horizontal plane, the far side of the head is slightly compressed, the near rounded feet show a tiny suggestion of their end/sole. The back of her head rests down, arms lie loosely outward beside the torso; bunny ears flop/rest backward. She is quiet and limp like a small rag doll laid on a table, not standing, seated, airborne or propped on elbows. Do not draw the table.
Keep the giant rounded-square head, just two smooth outer hair lobes and one curved fringe, two bunny ears, tiny simple bow, one circle-with-X button eye, one solid tiny diamond missing eye with two short stitches, plain trapezoid dress with one U-shaped apron line, rounded short arms and two rounded feet. No additional details, facial expression, fingers, hair strands, ruffles, cuffs or seams. Same tiny needle and thread spool resting separately beside the lower body, reduced to just a few lines.
Whole figure complete and uncropped, centered, fills about 82% of square canvas width, comfortable clear margins. Single-color ink, flat unfilled interiors, true transparent RGBA background including inside outline areas. No shading, shadows, ground, color fills, texture, background, text or watermark. Preserve very simple icon legibility at 104px.

Use case: style-transfer.
Create ONE minimal hand-drawn HEDGEHOG PINCUSHION character for a small portfolio icon. Image 1 is SUBJECT reference only: use the recognizable plump fabric pincushion hedgehog with a smooth dome back, long gently pointed snout, tiny round nose, tiny bead eyes and soft little ears, with sewing pins sticking out of its back. Image 2 is STYLE reference only: match its extremely simple, medium-bold, slightly wobbly rounded peacock-green #086B68 outline and sparse shapes. Do not depict the doll.
Draw a side/very slight three-quarter view facing LEFT. One large smooth rounded dome for the body, one pointed soft snout, a dot nose and a dot eye, one small curved ear, a simple curved division between the face and dome. Just FIVE well-spaced straight sewing pins with tiny round ball heads stick outward from the back in different directions, clearly readable and not a dense cluster. No natural spines or zigzag fur. Two tiny rounded feet in a gentle stepping pose give it a quietly alive, inquisitive feeling.
Only essential contour lines, no stitches, fabric texture, shading, whiskers, extra decorations, labels, scenery or other sewing supplies. Single peacock-green ink, unfilled interiors, TRUE transparent RGBA background throughout. Match line thickness and informal pen feel of image 2. Complete uncropped silhouette centered with 8–10% padding, filling about 82% of a square canvas width. Must remain immediately recognizable at 104px.

Keep the climber large and centered with this wall line as one compact complete illustration, character fills about 86% of square canvas height with small clear margins; do not miniaturize the person to make room for a large wall.
